page: Microsoft Azure D32pls_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine powered by a dedicated Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor. It features 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 3.4 GHz, with 1.0 thread per core. The memory configuration consists of 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. This instance does not include local storage or GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 25%. Memory subsystem performance is a notable strength; both large-block read and write memory bandwidth benchmarks rank in the top 10%, complemented by a top-tier PassMark memory score. Database operations also perform in the top 10%. However, single-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench remains in the middle 50%, and large-model LLM inference prompt processing is limited, falling into the bottom 10%.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio offers a resource-dense configuration for compute-heavy workloads that do not require large memory footprints, providing qualitative cost efficiency by avoiding over-provisioned RAM. Given the strong multi-threaded decompression, software compilation, and database operation benchmarks, this server is suited for multi-threaded application hosting, static web serving, software development pipelines, and database tasks that fit within the 64.0 GB memory limit.
